title: Following a Plan: Path Tracking and Reactive Obstacle Avoidance

contract.reader: An engineer or student who has followed entries 1 to 4 and knows basic feedback, about to make a mobile robot follow a plan
contract.problem: A plan computed once from a map meets a robot that slips, lags and meets obstacles the map did not show
contract.outcome: Write the unicycle and wheel equations; tune pure pursuit from its linearization; implement the Kanayama law and choose its gains; reproduce the traps of potential fields and DWA; place both in a layered navigation system with replanning and recovery
contract.contribution: One simulated differential-drive robot with lag, turn-rate limit and 20 Hz control on which each controller is run and its numbers explained by a linear model
contract.evidence: Derivations, programs with real output, Brockett 1983, Khatib 1986, Kanayama et al. 1990, Coulter 1992, Fox et al. 1997, Gat 1998 and others (numbers recomputed in the 2026-10-24 live review)
contract.limitations: Pose estimate taken as exact; kinematic model with one lag; static obstacles; DWA simplified

findings.location: Section 1, layers Mermaid diagram, edges between Wheel speed control and Robot and environment; mobile-light-06, mobile-dark-06, desktop
findings.problem: Edge labels 'motor current' and 'wheel encoders' overlap; the first reads 'motor curr'
findings.whyItMatters: The figure frames the entry and the lowest loop's labels collide
findings.action: Change the layout so the two edges separate (or move labels into nodes) and check both widths and themes
findings.acceptance: Both labels fully readable on new captures at 1280 and 360 px, light and dark
